summary: Lean backend-only retest (pytest/curl only, no browser) of the audio-storage GDPR delete work. Created /app/backend/tests/test_iter106_audio_delete_lean.py — 12 tests, ALL PASSING in ~100s. P1: put_audio -> get_audio (byte-exact) -> delete_audio against REAL Supabase Storage; object confirmed gone at origin (object/info returns 404 NoSuchKey, list empty) and a never-downloaded object 404s on get_audio after delete; delete_audio on a non-existent path is a no-op (no raise). P2: meeting with transcript+analysis+audio_files row -> GET /api/meetings/{id} returns analysis summary and transcript-text -> DELETE returns 200, GET now 404, meetings/transcripts/analyses/audio_files rows all 0, and the real Supabase object is purged; deleting a meeting with no audio_files row also 200 (clean skip); non-existent meeting 404. P3: information_schema confirms fk_evidence_feedback_meeting_id + fk_evidence_feedback_org_id exist; a raw DB delete of the parent meeting cascades the evidence_feedback row away (proves FK cascade, not just app-level cleanup). P4 smoke: admin/manager/jane logins (MFA override for manager), GET /api/dashboard/, GET /api/meetings/, GET /api/meetings/{id}, GET /api/review/{id}, audit-trail — no 500s, backend error log clean. Residue check: 0 DB rows and 0 Supabase objects left behind. Per the request, the 5-min grace-period timing test and full org-deletion e2e were NOT re-run; replaced with code review of the wiring (see notes).

minor.issue: GDPR edge-case: uploads don't set cache-control, so Supabase CDN caches objects with the default max-age (3600s). Verified reproducibly: an object that was downloaded once and then deleted still returns HTTP 200 with the audio bytes from the edge cache (cf-cache-status: HIT), even with Cache-Control: no-cache on the request, while the origin correctly reports 404. Deletion at origin is genuinely correct, but a previously-streamed recording can remain retrievable via the CDN for up to an hour after the GDPR purge. Suggest passing file_options={'cache-control': 'no-store'} (or max-age=0) on put_audio, and/or serving audio via short-lived signed URLs.

action_items: Optional (minor): set cache-control no-store/max-age=0 on put_audio so deleted audio can't be served from the Supabase CDN edge cache for up to 1h after a GDPR purge.
critical_code_review_comments: review.py delete_audio_after_grace(): delete_audio(storage_path) is correctly awaited BEFORE the audio_files/meetings flag updates, and the whole block is inside try/except, so a storage failure leaves audio_deletion_status='grace_period' and the row retryable by the sweep — wiring verified by reading, not re-timed (5-min sleep skipped as agreed).

job_worker._sweep_audio_deletions(): same ordering (storage delete then flag flip), per-row try/except so one failing object doesn't block others, and the query filters on status='grace_period' AND grace_period_started_at < cutoff AND status='signed_off' — idempotent and safe to re-run.

meetings.delete_meeting(): fetches storage_path list BEFORE the row delete and purges storage after the DB transaction, with per-path try/except + error log. Note the paths query filters is_deleted = FALSE, so an audio_files row flagged deleted but whose object failed to purge earlier will never be retried by meeting deletion — leaked-object risk is small but real; consider dropping that filter (delete_audio is idempotent on missing paths, confirmed by test).
init_db.py: both evidence_feedback FKs use ON DELETE CASCADE with duplicate_object/foreign_key_violation guards — present and active in the live DB (verified via information_schema + cascade probe).
seed_data_creation: Transient only, all cleaned up: TEST_iter106_ prefixed meetings/transcripts/analyses/audio_files rows and TEST_iter106_storage/ Supabase objects. Also cleaned one leftover TEST_iter106_storage object from an aborted first run.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Use /app/backend/tests/test_iter106_audio_delete_lean.py (fast, ~100s, run with -n 0) as the regression suite for audio GDPR deletion + evidence_feedback FK cascade. The heavier suite /app/backend/tests/test_iter105_audio_gdpr_delete.py covers grace-period task, recovery sweep, storage-failure retryability and org deletion but takes long (that's what timed out); run it selectively by class if needed. Supabase storage truth must be checked via /storage/v1/object/info/... or /object/list (origin), NOT via download — the CDN serves stale 200s for previously-downloaded deleted objects.
rca_of_the_issue: Two initial test failures were test-harness artifacts, not product bugs: (1) Supabase /object/list returns names relative to the prefix, so the full-path assertion failed (fixed in test); (2) get_audio() on a just-deleted path returned 200 because of the Supabase CDN edge cache (cf-cache-status HIT) — origin info/list correctly reported 404, and a never-downloaded object does 404 after delete. Recorded as a minor GDPR hardening item rather than a delete defect.
